thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1718234567 - decode-prod pool gpu-0 reporting recurrent CUDA OOMs during streaming decode. 90s avg OOM rate spike. Auto-scaler attempted restart -> crashes observed. Paging oncall: @Emma (oncall)

Emma (oncall): I'm on it. seeing alert in datadog. symptoms? request drops or retries?

incident-bot: Recent failures: 1) CUDA OOM at kernel launch, 2) container restart loop on node ip-10-4-12-33, 3) 502/timeout spikes for streaming endpoints. Last 10m errors: 16% dropped streams, 23% increased tail latency.

Emma (oncall): OK allocating paging channel. @Sanjay can you check node health and GPU memory logs? I'll start mitigation playbook.

Sanjay (infra): pulling kube events and container logs. node shows frequent oom_kill for process pid=4123 (decode-server). GPU memory usage maxed near 100% before OOM. There's a handful of long-running requests with max_tokens=20000.

Jake (sre): long generations. we've seen runaway max_tokens misconfigs cause this before. Any recent deploy or config change?

Maria (product): No deploys to serving config in last 2 hours. But Customer A mentioned large-batch prompts in their last run. CS notified them to pause. @Olivia, are we seeing support tickets?

Olivia (support): yes ticket #CS-9821 about huge outputs; customer ran a single request with max_tokens=50000. They thought the API would cap. They hit it ~5m before spike.

Emma (oncall): Good find. Immediate mitigation: enforce a temporary ingress max_tokens cap and enable token-based rate-limit for decode-prod. Applying iptables is risky; prefer config change in gateway. @ops-bot kick off config update to rate-limit and set server-side max_tokens=4096 for streaming route.

ops-bot: Running change: update route /v1/decode/streaming -> set max_tokens_limit=4096, per-customer burst limit=5 concurrent streams, global throttle=200rps. Rolling config to edge nodes now.

Sanjay (infra): While that rolls, I'll cordon the noisy node ip-10-4-12-33 and drain pods to avoid repeated restarts. suggested: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data ip-10-4-12-33.

Emma (oncall): Proceed. Also restart decode-server pods on remaining nodes to clear fragmented GPU memory. Use graceful restart to let in-flight finish within 30s.

Sanjay (infra): Draining node now. One caveat: a few pods failed to move due to eviction limits. I'm increasing pod disruption budget temporarily.

Jake (sre): Checking logs from failing container. snippet: 

```
2024-06-xxT13:45:12Z ERROR decode: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: an illegal memory access was encountered
2024-06-xxT13:45:12Z ERROR decode: traceback: RuntimeError: CUDA OOM at allocate 1342177280 bytes
... kv cache size=68MB, seq_len=16384, requested_out_tokens=32768
```

Jake (sre): That points to runaway sequence length + kv cache growth. Even with quantization we blow past device mem.

Emma (oncall): Good. After drain and gateway cap, we should see errors drop. Need quick customer impact calc: Olivia, estimate % of requests impacted and affected customers.

Olivia (support): Looking at last 30m: 1.2k streaming sessions started, ~180 dropped (15%). Top affected customers: Customer A (35% of dropped), Internal QA (10%), others more distributed. I've emailed Customer A to pause heavy jobs; they're acknowledging.

Maria (product): We'll need to add a soft quota and a user-visible warning in API when max_tokens > 4096. Also prompt docs update. But short-term, throttling is fine.

ops-bot: Gateway change completed on 5/6 edge nodes. new limits active.

Sanjay (infra): Node drained and marked unschedulable. Restarting remaining decode-server replicas with graceful drain. Rolling restarts in progress.

Emma (oncall): Monitoring errors now. Datadog dash: dropped streams fall to 3% in last 5m, OOM logs reduce to single-digit events. Latency stabilizing.

Jake (sre): Follow-up: schedule a model-level guardrail to cap effective sequence length at runtime and reject before allocation. Also add KV cache footprint estimate in admission check. File a ticket: INF-1427.

Olivia (support): Noted. I'm drafting a customer notification summarizing what happened, who was affected, and mitigations. Sending to legal & CS for review.

Emma (oncall): Thanks team. I'll keep the incident open for a 2hr post-mortem watch. Action items: 1) INF-1427 model guardrails (Jake), 2) API warning & docs (Maria), 3) permanent gateway limit + per-customer quotas (Sanjay/ops), 4) Customer comms (Olivia).

Maria (product): Also recommend a feature: server-side default max_tokens for accounts with no explicit limit to avoid accidental huge runs. Adding to roadmap.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to S2. Incident channel created: #inc-1718234567-streaming-gpu-oom. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/streaming-gpu-oom

Emma (oncall): Closing active mitigation now; keeping watch. Will open a follow-up postmortem doc in #postmortems in 24h. :thumbsup:
